body:
# The Mūt file: from mot to the temple it became
The domain you're reading about exists because someone refused to let **Mūt** stay *mot*.

Mōt's mythology is the dark season of the year made personal. His stories are preserved in the Baꜥal Cycle, where he confronts Baꜥal, kills him, and is in turn destroyed and reborn in a cycle that explains drought, death, and the return of fertility. In KTU 1. 4 vii–viii, Mōt sends word to Baꜥal: because he was not invited to the storm-god's feast, he will feast on Baꜥal himself.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Mūt
- **ASCII form:** mot
- **Meaning:** "Death"
- **Domain of influence:** Death, Underworld
- **Pantheon:** Phoenician
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** 𐤌𐤕
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 159 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

Strip **Mūt** to *mot* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **o → ū** — Macron: long /uː/ (Mūt): the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

These are the small, provable things a restoration is made of: not taste, not branding — attestation.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Mūt** lives at [/sites/mot/](/sites/mot/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/mot/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/mot/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/mot/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Mūt** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Funerary & Memorial Services** — Death itself in the Ugaritic cycle.
- **Agriculture, Food & Harvest** — The dry season personified; his grip on Baꜥal is the drought the harvest fears.
- **Gaming, Fantasy & Entertainment IP** — Modern fantasy and games cast him as the Canaanite lord of the underworld; death with a throne.

If a match here reads wrong, the atlas says how to challenge it. The patterns are falsifiable — that is what makes them worth publishing.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/mot/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.

Continue the series — previous file: **Mōšeh** ([read it here](/sites/moses/blog/restoration/)) · next file: **Muspellheimr** ([read it here](/sites/muspellheimr/blog/restoration/)).

*The Restoration Files are written from the same canonical record as the temples themselves: the lexicon, the lore catalog, the pattern atlas, and the cited scholarly sources. If a file ever disagrees with its temple, the temple is right — tell us, and the file will be corrected.*
